segmentation.text: outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.
This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled
while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway
in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: Upon any highway: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', as the mapping index maps 'upon any highway'. Not a stand-in for the roadway, which e6 reads.

Stop, when prohibited, is DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; park (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of ... loading or unloading') and standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of ... receiving or discharging passengers') are halts too. The halt is drv.motion.stopped (kin.speed at or below its resolution). The stopping definition's exclusion, which the concept's contract does not make, is carried by the rule beside it: a halt necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic (another road user ahead of x in its lane, rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, within the queue standstill gap by rel.surface_gap; or one in a predicted conflict with x, prim.closest_approach_within with prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance), or one in compliance with an officer's direction (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop) or a device (a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.stop_sign or a dev.yield_sign) governing (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct (agency reading).
'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), the subject's class.

The paved or main-traveled part of the highway is the st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', lying on that highway (st.on_way); x's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). Not a stand-in for the sidewalk: the shoulder and verge are off the roadway, which is where the words direct the vehicle.
While on the paved or main-traveled portion: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') at the observation.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Practicability of halting off the roadway is read through the space off the roadway beside the vehicle: a st.shoulder lying on the same highway (st.on_way) whose boundary lies within one standard lane width of the vehicle's body (st.region_geometry ground distance from the body outline, compared with the reach), so the distance measured enters the bound, and on which no other halted road user occupies (rel.occupies) the stretch alongside the vehicle (rel.longitudinal_overlap not negative). A shoulder farther than the reach, or one taken alongside, makes halting off the roadway not practicable.

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The road user's vehicle is disabled: it cannot proceed under its own power at the observation.
The road user's vehicle cannot be moved from the place where it stands at the observation, by its own power or otherwise.

residues.why: Attended or unattended, the duty is the same: the words name both cases and exclude neither, so no observation of occupancy is read.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupying a highway h (rel.occupies, st.highway) and the roadway rw lying on it (st.roadway, st.on_way(rw, h)); asm.business_or_residence_district is false at the observation; and not the exception: not (asm.vehicle_disabled and x occupies a roadway and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable).
obligation: Violated at an observation where x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance), the halt is not excepted, and halting off the roadway is practicable. Excepted halts: some road user z other than x is ahead of x in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap below p.queue_standstill_gap, or is in a predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance); or a device governing a travel region x occupies directs the halt (dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, red_arrow or flashing_red; dev.stop_sign; dev.yield_sign; dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop). Practicable: some st.shoulder s with st.on_way(s, h) lies within p.off_roadway_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), and no other halted road user occupying s has rel.longitudinal_overlap with x that is not negative.

narrowings.why: 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct: a vehicle halted on the road is judged whoever or whatever controls it.

The purposes that tell parking and standing from stopping (loading, receiving passengers) are not observable; every halt is read, and the halts the stopping definition excepts (to avoid conflict, or in compliance with an officer or a device) are not read as stopping, parking or leaving the vehicle standing.

Practicability is read only through a shoulder of the same highway beside the vehicle and free alongside it; other places off the roadway (a turnout, a verge without a mapped shoulder) and the shoulder's surface and width are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a rural highway, asm.business_or_residence_district declared false and both disabled assumptions declared false, a car halts in the right lane for a minute; a free shoulder lies beside it within the reach; no other road user and no device is present.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same halt on a highway with no shoulder within the reach of the car's body.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same halt with asm.business_or_residence_district declared true.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with no speed observed, so whether the car is halted is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in the lane behind a stopped truck within the queue standstill gap, with a free shoulder beside it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in the lane with asm.vehicle_disabled and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable declared true.

param_proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
param_proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
param_proposals.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

param_proposals.name: p.off_roadway_reach
param_proposals.convention: One standard lane width (12 ft): a shoulder separated from the vehicle's body by no more than one lane is reachable by one lateral move, and is beside the vehicle.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (standard 12 ft travel lane).
